fail_samples.text_head: NTA AND INVESTMENT UPDATE October 2026 Fund Performance Cadence Opportunities Fund was down 3.3% in September, compared to the All Ordinaries Accumulation Index which was up 0.7% for the month. The largest detractors from performance during the month were Turaco Gold, Cyprium Metals, Lindian Resources, Broken Hill Mines, Aeris Resources and Samsung Electronics. The top contributors were CSL, Many Peaks Minerals, Monday.com, FleetPartners and Pro Medicus. Broken Hill Mines (ASX Code: BHM) is a zinc, silver and gold producer in the Broken Hill region of NSW. Over the past couple of years, BHM acquired established infrastructure, old legacy mines and nearby targets, which it is proposing to consolidate into a regional hub. The company is currently in the ramp up phase, with the September quarter softer than expected operationally and compounded by softer commodity prices. We reduced our BHM exposure in October. FleetPartners (ASX Code: FPR) is one of Australia’s largest providers of vehicle leasing and fleet management services. FPR is one of several relatively inexpensive stocks on the ASX in recent times that has been subject to takeover activity. In August, FPR received a non-binding offer from SG Fleet valuing FPR at $3.60 per share. By October, after multiple parties entering the takeover battle and several subsequent bids, FPR entered into a Binding Implementation Scheme with SG Fleet for a total consideration of $5.30/sh, an 85% premium to where the stock was trading before the initial offer. In a little over 2 years MPK has acquired the early-stage exploration tenements from Turaco Gold & Predictive Discovery and delineated a Mineral Resource of over 2 million ounces. The gold endowment continues to expand with each drilling campaign. A scoping study to prove up the economics of the project is expected later this year. Across the alternative asset market, conditions remain mixed, with the WAM Alternative Assets investment team and our specialist investment partners continuing to take a selective approach to new opportunities. Private equity remains particularly selective, with the opportunities being identified by our investment partners not always meeting the return hurdles required to deploy capital. Real estate continues to present a strong pipeline of opportunities. Higher interest rates are placing pressure on some asset owners and capital structures, creating opportunities for investors with patient capital to acquire high-quality assets from distressed or motivated sellers. Within water, rainfall during October was higher than expected, although spot water prices have remained relatively resilient. El Niño conditions continue to be an important consideration for the water market, with the potential for drier conditions to support demand and pricing as the season progresses. One private equity investment in the WAM Alternative Assets investment portfolio is Apiam Animal Health (Apiam), held through specialist investment partner Adamantem Capital. Apiam is a veterinary and animal health services provider with a network of over 60 companion and mixed animal clinics. The business has a leading market position in regional Australia and a growing presence in metropolitan locations, providing care for companion, equine and production animals, alongside other ancillary services. Adamantem Capital's investment thesis centres on expanding Apiam's clinic network, improving veterinarian productivity and increasing the standard of care across the business. Apiam was previously listed on the ASX before being acquired by Adamantem Capital, providing an example of the take-private opportunities increasingly being considered by private equity managers. Through its specialist investment partners, WAM Alternative Assets can gain exposure to formerly listed businesses where private ownership provides managers with the opportunity to pursue operational improvements and longer-term value creation away from public markets. Renewable energy and carbon abatement company LGI (ASX: LGI) was a contributor to the investment portfolio performance, while electrical technologies and digital infrastructure specialist SKS Technologies Group (ASX: SKS) was a detractor. LGI’s share price increased in October following the acquisition of two operational solar farms in Queensland for $22 million. The Chinchilla and Brigalow solar farms provide a combined export capacity of 42 megawatts and are expected to contribute between $2.1 million and $4.0 million in annual earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) at current electricity prices. The acquisition accelerates LGI’s strategy to diversify beyond landfill gas, expanding its medium-term renewable energy platform to approximately 125 megawatts across biogas generation, solar generation and battery storage. The WAM Microcap investment team remain positive about LGI’s medium-term growth outlook given its significant development pipeline and ability to leverage its existing operating capabilities across an increasingly diversified portfolio of renewable energy assets. SKS Technologies Group’s (SKS) share price declined during October following weaker investor sentiment towards data centre-related companies, and a substantial sell-down by the company’s senior executives. Weaker investor sentiment was driven by the withdrawal of Firmus Technologies' initial public offering (IPO), as well as the delay of AirTrunk's IPO in Singapore and power connection for NEXTDC's M3 data centre in Melbourne. This caused the share price to weaken, despite SKS reaffirming its FY2027 outlook for profit before tax of $60 million. During October, Jinks family, SKS's founders and senior executives, also sold 10 million shares. This represented approximately 30% of their holding, with the Jinks family retaining around 21% of the company following the transaction. Inflation and the prospect of further Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) rate rises remained in focus, while concerns around the funding and capital intensity of artificial intelligence (AI) investment weighed on global semiconductor and data centre stocks. During the month, retirement income specialist Challenger (ASX: CGF) and diversified property company GPT Group (ASX: GPT) were contributors to the investment portfolio outperformance. Challenger’s share price rose strongly following the announcement of an $11.80 per share non-binding takeover proposal from TAL Daiichi Life Australia, which owns approximately 20.5% of the company. GPT Group’s share price was supported by a strong rally in long-dated Australian bonds during the month, reversing much of the weakness seen in September and improving sentiment towards long- duration property assets. Operationally, the $200 million Rouse Hill Town Centre expansion opened fully leased, adding 10,500 square metres and more than 50 tenancies with income accruing from day one. The development is tracking to a yield on cost ahead of its initial 6.5% target. The successful delivery demonstrates GPT Group’s ability to create value through its development pipeline. The investment team remains constructive on GPT Group’s high-quality portfolio and improving earnings fundamentals, with the share price continuing to trade at a discount to its net tangible asset backing.
